title: DQAOA-GPT: AI-Accelerated Distributed Quantum Optimization for Combinatorial Problems
authors: Seongmin Kim, Abhinav Rijal, Yuri Alexeev, Nora Bauer, Martin Roetteler, Mina Yoon, George Siopsis, In-Saeng Suh
abstract: While combinatorial optimization problems are central to many scientific and engineering applications, their solution remains challenging due to exponentially large search spaces. Variational quantum algorithms offer a promising route for tackling such problems, yet their practical performance is limited by repeated quantum circuit evaluations and classical parameter updates. In this work, we introduce DQAOA-GPT, a hybrid framework that integrates the distributed quantum approximate optimization algorithm (DQAOA), which decomposes a large optimization problem into smaller sub-problems, with GPT-based quantum circuit generation for solving those sub-problems. Rather than relying on iterative variational optimization, the proposed approach uses a trained generative model to directly generate high-quality quantum circuits for the decomposed sub-problems. As a benchmark, we evaluate DQAOA-GPT against conventional DQAOA on dense HUBO optimization problems with up to 100 decision variables. The results demonstrate that DQAOA-GPT significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining competitive solution quality, with larger acceleration observed for larger sub-problem sizes. Although this work focuses on benchmark-scale validation, the framework provides a promising foundation for larger-scale combinatorial optimization in hybrid HPC-QC environments through increased GPU resources and parallel computing capability.
summary: This paper introduces DQAOA-GPT, a hybrid framework that accelerates solving hard combinatorial problems by replacing iterative quantum circuit optimization with direct circuit generation using a GPT model. By leveraging this AI acceleration during problem decomposition, the method drastically reduces computational cost while maintaining high solution quality for large-scale instances.
main_problem: Solving large-scale, NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that are intractable using standard variational quantum algorithms.
main_result: The proposed DQAOA-GPT significantly reduces the computational cost of solving sub-problems compared to conventional DQAOA while maintaining competitive solution quality, especially for larger problem sizes.
method: It integrates Distributed QAOA (DQAOA) with a GPT model that is trained to directly generate high-quality quantum circuits for decomposed sub-problems in a single inference pass.
model_or_system: The framework uses DQAOA to decompose the large optimization problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems. These sub-problems are then encoded onto graphs and solved using parameterized quantum circuits generated by the GPT model.
key_observables: Solution quality (accuracy) and computational runtime/cost reduction relative to conventional DQAOA.
important_parameters: Sub-problem size ($n$), number of variables ($N=100$ benchmark), and the depth/structure of the generated quantum circuits.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that decomposing the problem into smaller, locally optimized sub-problems is sufficient for finding a near-optimal global solution. The GPT model replaces iterative optimization with direct generation.
figures_summary: Figure 3 shows that DQAOA-GPT maintains relatively constant runtime while achieving improved relative accuracy as the sub-problem size ($n$) increases, contrasting sharply with standard DQAOA's rapidly increasing cost.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the difficulty of combinatorial optimization. It then details the DQAOA decomposition strategy and introduces the GPT training pipeline (tokenization, transformer architecture). Finally, it presents the inference loop where the generated circuits are used within the DQAOA framework for benchmarking.
why_interesting: While focused on optimization rather than fundamental AMO physics, the reliance on quantum circuit generation via a generative AI model represents a novel computational paradigm that could accelerate simulations or parameter estimation in complex open quantum systems.
